episodes.206711: Subtropical moisture associated with the remnants of Hurricane Priscilla in the eastern Pacific moved across northwest New Mexico on October 10th resulting in scattered shower and thunderstorm activity across this part of the state. Thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding in the normally dry Estes Arroyo northwest of Aztec. These floodwaters washed away a vehicle driving through the arroyo at County Road 3078. Thankfully, the occupant of the vehicle was rescued by a county fire and rescue crew and sustained no injuries.
episodes.206773: Remnant moisture from two tropical cyclones, Priscilla and Raymond moved into the state of Arizona.  Two west coast troughs interacted with this remnant moisture and provided ample lift and shear for heavy rain and severe thunderstorms.  The rain led to creek and stream level rises and some flash flooding.
episodes.207129: An extended duration local nor'easter wind event developed October 9th and persisted through the 12th between high pressure wedging down the SE US coast and a sharpening coastal trough axis over the local coastal waters. Gusty winds of 40-51 mph impacted coastal areas, with the strongest winds from 10/9 in the afternoon through 10/10 in the evening along the Duval county coast of 51 mph. Tidal flooding reached moderate levels along the coast, Intracoastal Waterway and inland within the St. Johns River and its tributaries 10/10 through 10/12. This inundation flooded roads and surrounded some vulnerable homes with flood water around high tides. Waves of showers moved onshore with localized flooding rainfall.
episodes.207225: A surge of moisture brought flash flooding to southern Utah.
episodes.207557: Gale-force wind gusts occurred along the oceanside of Key West as a break wake low pressure system formed from a cluster of strong thunderstorms over the Straits of Florida.
episodes.207894: The remnants of Pacific Hurricane Priscilla pushed tropical moisture into southern Nevada, fueling scattered thunderstorms. Several produced heavy rain and flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
episodes.207995: Locally heavy rainfall entered several homes in Volusia County, causing minor damage, and led to road closures in Palm Bay in Brevard County, while high astronomical tides and coastal flooding led to damage at the shoreline.
episodes.208116: A wet, unstable weather pattern due to Tropical Storm Jerry's proximity supports periods of heavy rain and thunderstorm activity across PR.
episodes.208261: A compact low pressure system passing directly over Lake Superior lead to a brief storm force gust out of the northwest behind the low on the evening of the 10th.
episodes.208421: A frontal boundary slowly moving across the region, sufficient low-level moisture, and astronomically higher-than-normal high tides combined to create a scenario where localized flooding emerged on the evening of October 9th into the 10th over portions of Southeast Florida.

events.narrative: A house near Mae Road was struck by lightning, knocking off the siding and scorching the house, but not setting fire to it.

Zion National Park reported mud and sand covering SR-9 at the Washington-Kane County line after heavy rainfall. Heavy equipment was required to clear the road. There were reports of numerous washouts in dry washes and slot canyons on the east side of Zion National Park. The USGS river gauge on the North Fork of the Virgin River reported a sharp rise from a baseline of 45 cfs to 869 cfs within 15 minutes. Zion National Park reported high flows on Clear Creek.
Florida DOT reported that SR-786, locally known as PBA Boulevard, was closed from SR-710 to Ryder Cup Boulevard in Palm Beach Gardens due to water from heavy rains on the  roadway.
A USGS stream gauge in Jacks Canyon (JCCA3) measured a 5.4 foot rise from widespread rainfall of 0.75 to 1.25 inches upstream.  Peak flow was 699 cfs.
A USGS stream gauge on the East Verde River (EVDA3) reported over a 2 foot rise in 90 minutes.  That's an increase in flow from 12 to 630 cfs.

Volusia County Emergency Management reports that flooding due to heavy rainfall entered twenty-four homes in Edgewater. The area impacted spread from W Knapp Ave and Palmetto St to just south of 30th St and Yule Tree Dr. Flooding was exacerbated by saturated soils and reduced drainage capacity due to the ongoing king tide and coastal flooding event. Most of the damage reported was minor. In addition to water entering homes, multiple roadways were flooded, mainly in the Florida Shores area. Several roadways were closed. Rainfall totals between October 8th and 11th in Edgewater were up to 5 to 7 inches.
A personal weather station Hilltop - KGAAMBRO2  measured 3.72 inches of rain. Rain began around 730 AM. About 2 inches of rain fell  between 930 AM and 1030 AM.

The county EM reported ground truth rainfall around 6 inches in Ambrose with some road  washouts in normally flood prone areas in the city and on secondary dirt roads. The  location and time are approximate based on the EM report.
Street flooding reported along Federal Hwy and NE 56th St. Water depth approximately 6-8 inches.
Wilton Manors police department reported on social media that multiple roads are  experiencing flooding from heavy rainfall.
Street flooding on Commercial Boulevard reported due to heavy rainfall.

Law enforcement reported that Jupiter Blvd was flooded from Emerson Dr to Lynbrook St NW in Palm Bay. The road was closed at the intersection with Emerson Dr and between Banks St NW and Beacon St NW. In addition, there were several public photos of cars stalled in water up to the windows, with one at Wake Forest Rd NW and Barton Ave NW. High water rescue vehicles were deployed. Mesonet observations show accumulations of 4 to nearly 7 inches of rainfall.
Broadcast media reported street flooding on Pembroke Road in Hallandale. Report via  social media.

events.narrative: A southeast wind gust of 35 knots was recorded at Key West International Airport.
A vehicle was washed away in fast moving water several feet deep in the normally dry Estes Arroyo at County Road 3078. The single occupant in the vehicle was rescued without sustaining any injuries.
Navajo Nation Police reported that N6461/N6460 closed due to a washout and significant road damage west of the Loop Road. The exact time of the wash-out is unknown.
Emergency management reported that a lightning strike impacted a power pole and associated electrical lines along Calle 59 in the Rexville area of Bayam��n. No injuries were reported.

events.county: Manitou Island To Marquette Mi And W Of Grand Marais Mi To Us/Canadian Border Beyond 5Nm Of Shore
events.narrative: The University of Michigan mesonet station STKM4 Stannard Rock Lighthouse measured a brief NW wind gust of 60 mph at 4 PM EST on the 10th.
The West Clear Creek stream gauge near Camp Verde (WCLA3) recorded a rapid 6.5 ft rise.  That's an increase in flow from 48 to 6039 cfs.

The Wet Beaver Creek  stream gauge near Rimrock (WBVA3) showed a rapid rise from 2.89 feet at 3 pm to peak in the Moderate Flood Stage category at 11.11 feet at 3:30 pm.  This is a rise in flow from 12 to 5068 cfs.
Rain in the Las Vegas Valley led to flowing water in the Harmon Wash, leading to a swift water rescue of two women in the wash. One man in the wash is still missing and presumed dead.
Rain in the Las Vegas Valley led to flowing water in the washes. A swift water rescue of someone in the wash occurred behind Rosewater Drive in Henderson.
